guide.biology: A glass or plastic divider splits one pond into separate pools that no longer share water.
guide.rules: A wall cell blocks everything: food, gases and organisms cannot cross it, and it holds nothing. It cannot cross the rim or cover a live organism. Whatever was dissolved or lying in a covered cell is moved, whole, into the nearest open cells on the same side, so no material is lost or made; a pocket with no open neighbour cannot be sealed. Unlike stone, its edges are not an attachment surface. Erasing it brings back the substrate underneath. No additional modeled reaction.
guide.example: Close a wall across the dish, then compare the two sides: they become separate little worlds.
